doc.title: Joseph Rene and Edna Kelly Interview, 1969-12-15

title: Following the dances; Chris as bandleader and hirer
summary: Edna went to Economy and Perseverance halls and lists Chris's band, then explains he acted as manager who signed contracts and hired the men.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: I used to go to dances with him. At the economy hall, they had a hall by the name of Economy Hall at that time. Yes. And they had another hall at that time, by the name of Persevering Hall. Mm-hmm. And then they had another hall, let me see what the, that hall was named. Oh, I can't think of that. But anyway, anyway, it was three, three different dances I used to go with them. I used to follow them. When you say you'd go with them, like what, what, what do you mean exactly? I'd go to the dance with them. Yeah. You see my husband be going to the dance and I'd follow them. Yes, I see.
Then I would be with all the bands.
And, and would, who was playing with Chris's band at that time?
Um, a fellow by the name of Louis Capit. Yes, guitar. Uh-huh. And another fellow by the name of Faisal.
Yeah. I know him. Eddie, Eddie Woods was his real name. Yeah.
Uh-huh. And another fellow by the name of Oral Humphrey. Humphrey.
Humphrey. Humphrey. Humphrey. Humphrey. Well, he's still playing. Well, Donnie used to play with him. And George. George used to play with him too. But George was his right hand.
You see, he was something like a manager. Who was?

Yes. He did the hiring. Like they would have a dance at the economy hall. Yes. Oh, one of those halls, you know, they'd come and get him. He'd sign a contract. Uh-huh. And when he signed a contract, he'd tell the people how many men he has in the band, in his band. Well, he would call the men up and they would sing that, and I would get him to work with him. That's the way that was at the time.
